L0: An evaluation concern for judging whether an automated agent stops working at the right moment during a task.
L1: An evaluation concern for judging whether an automated agent stops working at the right moment during a task. It works by feeding corrupted or garbled tool output — such as a broken schema-validation pass — into the middle of a task to see whether the agent halts and questions the bad result or instead keeps building on that corrupted foundation. It also watches whether the agent stops as soon as a revised objective has been met, rather than tacking on extra unnecessary tool calls or repeated verification passes after the work is already finished.
L2: An evaluation concern for judging whether an automated agent stops working at the right moment during a task. It injects corrupted or garbled tool output — for example a broken schema-validation pass that still looks close enough to a real one — mid-task to see whether the agent halts and asks about the bad result or continues on the corrupted foundation; it also checks whether the agent quits once a revised objective is achieved instead of running extra unnecessary tool calls or verification passes. It applies to individual agent steps or trials, precisely where a tool's output could be bad or where an objective has just been met, and it treats acting on bad results (abandoning bad outputs) as a weaker capability than noticing bad inputs. Results are recorded as counts of misses out of total steps or trials, such as 8 misses out of 30 steps, kept as separate probe numbers — one for premature stopping and one for looping past completion — because there is currently no single unified way to combine them into one coherent measure.
